import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Smooth
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyOpen
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Grp
import Mathlib.RingTheory.SimpleRing.Principal
import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.RationalMapPrecomp
import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.RationalMapProd

/-!
# Milne's difference rational map `Φ = (x, y) ↦ f(x) · f(y)⁻¹`

This file assembles **Sub-step 1** of Milne's Lemma 3.3
(`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`):
from a rational map `f : X ⤏ G` into a group variety over an algebraically closed
field `k̄`, build the *difference rational map*

  `Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G`,   `Φ(x, y) = f(x) · f(y)⁻¹`,

which is the vehicle for reducing the indeterminacy of `f` to a pole-divisor
computation on the nonsingular surface `X ×_{k̄} X`.

The construction glues the two rational-map bricks already in the project:

* `Scheme.RationalMap.precomp` (`Albanese/RationalMapPrecomp.lean`) — precompose
  `f` with the two projections `prᵢ : X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X`, which are open because
  `X.hom` is smooth (hence its base change `prᵢ` is smooth, flat, locally of finite
  presentation, universally open, an open map);
* `Scheme.RationalMap.prod` (`Albanese/RationalMapProd.lean`) — pair
  `f ∘ pr₁` and `f ∘ pr₂` into `X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G ×_{k̄} G`;

and then composes on the right with the **group-object difference morphism**
`GrpObj.diff G = (g, h) ↦ g · h⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G`, whose underlying scheme morphism
`(GrpObj.diff G).left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` is the honest group law `m ∘ (id × inv)`.

The pairing `prod` requires the source `X ×_{k̄} X` to be integral; this is passed
as the hypothesis `[IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)]`. The caller supplies it via
the project lemma `isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed` (self-product is smooth over
`k̄`, hence reduced) together with `GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace` — the
`isIntegral_pullback_self` recipe is spelled out in the module note below and lives
in `CodimOneExtension.lean`'s cone (it depends on the standard-smooth chart machinery
there, so it is not restated here to keep this file a Mathlib-only leaf).

## Main definitions

* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.diff` — the division morphism `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` of a group
  object in any cartesian-monoidal category.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.grpObjDiffLeft` — its underlying scheme morphism, typed as
  `pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.differenceRationalMap` — Milne's
  `Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G`.

## Main results

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self` / `..._snd_self` — the two
  projections of the self-product are open maps.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.differenceRationalMap_compHom_over` — the
  difference map is a `k̄`-rational map (`Φ.compHom G.hom = (pr₁ ≫ X.hom).toRat`).

Sub-steps 2 (`(x, x) ∈ Dom Φ ↔ x ∈ Dom f`) and 4b (diagonal codim-1 Krull bound)
remain; they consume `differenceRationalMap` built here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonoidalCategory Limits TopologicalSpace
open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory.GrpObj

variable {C : Type*} [Category C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]

/-- **Difference / division morphism of a group object.** For a group object `G`
in a cartesian-monoidal category, `GrpObj.diff G = fst / snd : G ⊗ G ⟶ G` is the
morphism `(g, h) ↦ g · h⁻¹`, i.e. the group law composed with inversion on the
second factor. There is no ready-made such morphism in mathlib (`GrpObj.conj` and
`GrpObj.commutator` are the only prebuilt `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` maps), so we build it from
the hom-set group structure `CategoryTheory.MonObj.Hom.group`. -/
noncomputable def diff (G : C) [GrpObj G] : G ⊗ G ⟶ G :=
  fst G G / snd G G

/-- **Reconstruction identity `(a · b⁻¹) · b = a` for `T`-points of a group object.**
Pairing `a` and `b` into `G ⊗ G`, applying the difference `diff G = fst / snd`
(which sends `(a, b) ↦ a · b⁻¹`), pairing the result again with `b`, and multiplying
recovers `a`. This is the group-theoretic heart of Milne Lemma 3.3 Sub-step 2, the
formula `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`: with `a = f(x)`, `b = f(u)`, the difference map value
`Φ = a · b⁻¹` recombines with `b` to give `a`. -/
lemma lift_diff_lift_mul {T : C} (G : C) [GrpObj G] (a b : T ⟶ G) :
    lift (lift a b ≫ diff G) b ≫ μ = a := by
  rw [diff, GrpObj.comp_div, lift_fst, lift_snd]
  exact div_mul_cancel a b

end CategoryTheory.GrpObj

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar]

/-- The underlying scheme morphism `(GrpObj.diff G).left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` of the
group-object difference morphism, typed directly against `pullback G.hom G.hom`
(definitionally `(G ⊗ G).left` via `Over.tensorObj_left`). This coercion avoids the
`(G ⊗ G).left` vs `pullback G.hom G.hom` transparency wall when right-composing a
rational map with target `pullback G.hom G.hom`. -/
noncomputable def grpObjDiffLeft (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left :=
  (GrpObj.diff G).left

/-- The difference morphism sits over `Spec k̄`: `grpObjDiffLeft G ≫ G.hom =
pr₁ ≫ G.hom`. This is the reduction that turns `Φ.compHom G.hom` into the structure
morphism of `X ×_{k̄} X`; it is `Over.w` of `GrpObj.diff G`. -/
lemma grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    grpObjDiffLeft G ≫ G.hom = pullback.fst G.hom G.hom ≫ G.hom :=
  Over.w (GrpObj.diff G)

/-- The underlying scheme morphism `μ.left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` of the group law of `G`,
typed against `pullback G.hom G.hom` (definitionally `(G ⊗ G).left`), mirroring
`grpObjDiffLeft`. -/
noncomputable def grpObjMulLeft (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left :=
  (μ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G).left

/-- **Scheme-level reconstruction identity.** For two `k̄`-morphisms `A, B : T ⟶ G`
sharing the structure map `t` (`A ≫ G.hom = B ≫ G.hom = t`), pairing them, applying
the group difference `A · B⁻¹`, re-pairing with `B` and multiplying recovers `A`:
`m ∘ ⟨(A · B⁻¹), B⟩ = A`. This is `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.lift_diff_lift_mul`
transported through `Over.forget` (`(-).left` is a functor sending
`CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift`/`fst` to `pullback.lift`/`pullback.fst`); it is the
scheme incarnation of Milne's `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`. -/
lemma pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) (A B : T ⟶ G.left)
    (hA : A ≫ G.hom = t) (hB : B ≫ G.hom = t) :
    pullback.lift (pullback.lift A B (hA.trans hB.symm) ≫ grpObjDiffLeft G) B
        (by rw [Category.assoc, grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom, ← Category.assoc,
          pullback.lift_fst, hA, hB]) ≫ grpObjMulLeft G
      = A := by
  have key := congrArg (fun m : Over.mk t ⟶ G => m.left)
    (GrpObj.lift_diff_lift_mul G (Over.homMk A hA) (Over.homMk B hB))
  simp only [Over.comp_left, Over.lift_left, Over.homMk_left] at key
  exact key

/-- The first projection `X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X` is an open map (it is smooth, being a
base change of the smooth structure morphism, hence universally open). -/
theorem isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self (X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth X.hom] :
    IsOpenMap (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).base :=
  (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).isOpenMap

/-- The second projection `X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X` is an open map. -/
theorem isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self (X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth X.hom] :
    IsOpenMap (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).base :=
  (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).isOpenMap

namespace Scheme.RationalMap

/-- **Right-composition with a morphism only enlarges the domain of definition.**
For a rational map `F : X ⤏ Y` and a morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z`, every point at which
`F` is defined is also a point at which `F.compHom g` is defined: a partial-map
representative `F₀` of `F` yields the representative `F₀.compHom g` of
`F.compHom g` with the *same* domain (post-composing with a total morphism never
destroys definedness). This is Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 1: the difference map
`Φ = (prod ⋯).compHom (diff_G)` is defined wherever the pairing `prod ⋯` is. -/
theorem le_domain_compHom {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.RationalMap Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    F.domain ≤ (F.compHom g).domain := by
  intro x hx
  rw [RationalMap.mem_domain] at hx ⊢
  obtain ⟨F₀, hxF₀, hF₀⟩ := hx
  exact ⟨F₀.compHom g, hxF₀, by rw [RationalMap.compHom_toRationalMap, hF₀]⟩

variable {X G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
  [Smooth X.hom]
  [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom]

/-- **Milne's difference rational map** `Φ = (x, y) ↦ f(x) · f(y)⁻¹`.

For a rational map `f : X ⤏ G` into a group variety over `k̄`, with `f` defined
over `k̄` (`f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap`), the difference map
`Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G` is `((f ∘ pr₁) ×_{k̄} (f ∘ pr₂)) ∘ (g, h ↦ g · h⁻¹)`.

The self-product must be integral for the pairing `prod` to be well-defined; this
is the hypothesis `[IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)]`. -/
noncomputable def differenceRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (pullback X.hom X.hom).RationalMap G.left :=
  (RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
      (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
      (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap])
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
        pullback.condition])).compHom (grpObjDiffLeft G)

/-- **The difference map is a `k̄`-rational map.** Right-composing `Φ` with the
structure morphism `G.hom` recovers the structure morphism `pr₁ ≫ X.hom` of
`X ×_{k̄} X`. -/
theorem differenceRationalMap_compHom_over
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (differenceRationalMap f hover).compHom G.hom
      = (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom).toRationalMap := by
  simp only [differenceRationalMap]
  rw [RationalMap.compHom_compHom, grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom]
  exact RationalMap.prod_compHom_over _ _ _ _ _ _ _

/-- The explicit pairing partial map `U ×_{k̄} U → G ×_{k̄} G` of Milne's
construction (`(x, y) ↦ (φ_U(x), φ_U(y))`), built from the maximal representative
`φ_U = f.toPartialMap` of `f` over the common domain `Dom(f∘pr₁) ⊓ Dom(f∘pr₂)`. It
is the partial-map witness that `prod` is defined on `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`. -/
noncomputable def precompDiffPairing
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left) (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (pullback X.hom X.hom).PartialMap (pullback G.hom G.hom) where
  domain := (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
      (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain
    ⊓ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
      (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).domain
  dense_domain := by
    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_inf]
    exact (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).dense_domain.inter_of_isOpen_left
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).dense_domain
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain.isOpen
  hom := pullback.lift
    ((pullback X.hom X.hom).homOfLE inf_le_left
      ≫ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).hom)
    ((pullback X.hom X.hom).homOfLE inf_le_right
      ≫ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).hom)
    (by
      -- Over-`Spec k̄` structure making *both* projections `S`-morphisms (they agree
      -- after `X.hom` by `pullback.condition`), so the precomposed legs inherit
      -- over-ness from `f.toPartialMap` without ever unfolding `precomp`.
      letI : X.left.Over (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨X.hom⟩
      letI : G.left.Over (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨G.hom⟩
      letI : (pullback X.hom X.hom).Over (Spec (.of kbar)) :=
        ⟨pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom⟩
      haveI : f.IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := RationalMap.isOver_iff.mpr hover
      haveI : (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨rfl⟩
      haveI : (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨pullback.condition.symm⟩
      have e₁ : (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).hom ≫ G.hom
          = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain.ι ≫ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) :=
        (PartialMap.isOver_iff (S := Spec (.of kbar))).mp inferInstance
      have e₂ : (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).hom ≫ G.hom
          = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).domain.ι ≫ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) :=
        (PartialMap.isOver_iff (S := Spec (.of kbar))).mp inferInstance
      rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, e₁, e₂]
      simp only [← Category.assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_ι])

omit [GrpObj G] in
/-- The explicit pairing partial map represents Milne's `prod (f∘pr₁, f∘pr₂)`. Both
are `k̄`-rational maps out of the integral scheme `X ×_{k̄} X`, so it suffices to
match their induced morphisms `Spec K(X × X) ⟶ G ×_{k̄} G`: on each `pullback`
factor the pairing's generic-point morphism restricts to `(f ∘ prᵢ)`'s. -/
theorem precompDiffPairing_toRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (precompDiffPairing f hover).toRationalMap
      = RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
        (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
        (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap])
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
          pullback.condition]) := by
  refine RationalMap.eq_of_fromFunctionField_eq _ _ ?_
  rw [RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, prod_fromFunctionField]
  apply pullback.hom_ext
  · rw [pullback.lift_fst]
    have hrhs : (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField
        = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField := by
      rw [← RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, RationalMap.precomp_toRationalMap,
        f.toRationalMap_toPartialMap]
    rw [hrhs, ← PartialMap.fromFunctionField_restrict
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
      (precompDiffPairing f hover).dense_domain inf_le_left]
    simp only [PartialMap.fromFunctionField, PartialMap.fromSpecStalkOfMem,
      PartialMap.restrict_hom, Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
  · rw [pullback.lift_snd]
    have hrhs : (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField
        = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField := by
      rw [← RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, RationalMap.precomp_toRationalMap,
        f.toRationalMap_toPartialMap]
    rw [hrhs, ← PartialMap.fromFunctionField_restrict
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
      (precompDiffPairing f hover).dense_domain inf_le_right]
    simp only [PartialMap.fromFunctionField, PartialMap.fromSpecStalkOfMem,
      PartialMap.restrict_hom, Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 1 (domain lower bound / Sub-step 2 easy direction).**
The difference rational map `Φ` is defined on `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`: every point
`p` of `X ×_{k̄} X` projecting into `Dom(f)` under both projections lies in
`Dom(Φ)`. This is Milne's "clearly `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)` if `f` is defined at
`x`" — indeed at every `(x, y)` with `x, y ∈ Dom(f)` — made precise: a maximal
representative `(U, φ_U)` of `f` (`f.toPartialMap`) supplies the honest morphism
`U ×_{k̄} U → G` of Milne's construction, which represents `Φ`. -/
theorem le_domain_differenceRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain) ⊓ (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain)
      ≤ (differenceRationalMap f hover).domain := by
  -- Right-composition with `diff_G` only enlarges the domain, reducing to `prod`;
  -- the explicit pairing `precompDiffPairing` is a representative defined on all of
  -- `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`.
  refine le_trans ?_ (le_domain_compHom _ (grpObjDiffLeft G))
  intro p hp
  rw [RationalMap.mem_domain]
  exact ⟨precompDiffPairing f hover, hp, precompDiffPairing_toRationalMap f hover⟩

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 2 reconstruction identity.** `f ∘ pr₁ = m ∘ ⟨Φ, f ∘ pr₂⟩`:
the difference map `Φ = f(x)·f(y)⁻¹` recombined with the second factor `f ∘ pr₂` via the
group law `m` recovers the first factor `f ∘ pr₁`. This is Milne's formula
`f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`, made a rational-map identity on `X ×_{k̄} X` via the
function-field group law (`pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul`). -/
theorem reconstruct_precomp_fst
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
        (differenceRationalMap f hover)
        (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
        (differenceRationalMap_compHom_over f hover)
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
          pullback.condition])).compHom (grpObjMulLeft G)
      = f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X) := by
  refine RationalMap.eq_of_fromFunctionField_eq _ _ ?_
  rw [RationalMap.fromFunctionField_compHom, RationalMap.prod_fromFunctionField]
  simp only [differenceRationalMap, RationalMap.fromFunctionField_compHom,
    RationalMap.prod_fromFunctionField]
  exact pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul G _
    ((f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField)
    ((f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField)
    (RationalMap.fromFunctionField_comp_structure _ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap]))
    (RationalMap.fromFunctionField_comp_structure _ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
        pullback.condition]))

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 2 (hard direction, algebraic content).** `f ∘ pr₁` is
defined wherever `Φ` is defined *and* `f ∘ pr₂` is defined: at a point `p` with
`Φ` defined and `pr₂ p ∈ Dom(f)`, the reconstruction `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)` exhibits
`f ∘ pr₁` as regular. Concretely `Dom(Φ) ⊓ pr₂⁻¹(Dom f) ≤ Dom(f ∘ pr₁)`.

This is the group-theoretic half of Milne's converse (`(x, x) ∈ Dom Φ ⟹ x ∈ Dom f`);
it remains to combine it with the topological input — openness of `Dom(Φ)` and
irreducibility of the fibre `X_{κ(x)}` (geometric irreducibility) to produce a suitable
`u`, plus the smooth-descent reflection `Dom(f ∘ pr₁) ⊆ pr₁⁻¹(Dom f)`. -/
theorem le_domain_precomp_fst_of_difference
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (differenceRationalMap f hover).domain ⊓ (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain)
      ≤ (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain := by
  rw [← reconstruct_precomp_fst f hover]
  refine le_trans ?_ (le_domain_compHom _ (grpObjMulLeft G))

11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	**Status, measured (run 0069).** `albanese_universal_property` is *assembled*
54	from `descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`,
55	and that assembly is honest — but the headline is **not** sorry-free:
56	`#print axioms albanese_universal_property` reports `sorryAx`, inherited from
57	the six unproved declarations below. It should not be described as a landed
58	theorem until they close.
59	
60	### Read this first: the mathematics is proved *elsewhere in this directory*
61	
62	The six obligations below are stated against `SymmetricPower`, which is a
63	`sorry`-**bodied definition**. An equation between morphisms out of a junk term
64	carries no information, so these six cannot be discharged, and discharging them
65	would establish nothing. They are kept because they pin the challenge's intended
66	statement shape, not because they are the work.
67	
68	Milne's argument itself **is** proved, over the symmetric power taken as an
69	*interface* rather than a `sorry`:
70	
71	* `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean` — `SymPowData C n` (carrier, symmetrisation
72	  projection, universal property), and everything Milne derives from it:
73	  `SymPowData.symAVMap` (his `Sym^n φ`, now a **construction**),
74	  `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` (the collapse behind "use `φ(P₀) = η_A`"),
75	  and `symPowDataOne` — which **inhabits** the interface (`Sym^1 C = C`), so
76	  statements quantifying over it are not vacuous.
77	* `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` — the connector in **both** directions and the
78	  universal property assembled over the interface. Worth knowing: the backward
79	  direction needs neither the quotient property nor that `ψ` is a homomorphism;
80	  only the forward direction does.
81	* `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean` — commutativity of an abelian variety and pointed
82	  rigidity, on the project's four-instance package.
83	* `Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean` — the instantiation at `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`, plus a
84	  machine check attributing its `sorryAx` entirely to the Picard seam: the same
85	  theorem with an arbitrary abelian variety target is axiom-clean.
86	
87	So the honest description of this leg is **one missing object**, not six gaps:
88	`SymPowData C g` for `g ≥ 2`.

90	**Update (2026-07-28) — that object is now identified, and the missing part is smaller than

92	*together with* its symmetry hypothesis **is** a colimit of the `S_n`-action on `C^n`, in

95	* the symmetry half is `colimit.w` — free, at every `n`;
96	* the **affine algebra** case is *inhabited* at every `n` (`symPowData_affineAlgebra`, in

99	* what remains is the **gluing**, as one instance: `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` — the

This file assembles **Sub-step 1** of Milne's Lemma 3.3
(`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`):
from a rational map `f : X ⤏ G` into a group variety over an algebraically closed
field `k̄`, build the *difference rational map*

  `Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G`,   `Φ(x, y) = f(x) · f(y)⁻¹`,

which is the vehicle for reducing the indeterminacy of `f` to a pole-divisor
computation on the nonsingular surface `X ×_{k̄} X`.

The construction glues the two rational-map bricks already in the project:

* `Scheme.RationalMap.precomp` (`Albanese/RationalMapPrecomp.lean`) — precompose
  `f` with the two projections `prᵢ : X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X`, which are open because
  `X.hom` is smooth (hence its base change `prᵢ` is smooth, flat, locally of finite
  presentation, universally open, an open map);
* `Scheme.RationalMap.prod` (`Albanese/RationalMapProd.lean`) — pair
  `f ∘ pr₁` and `f ∘ pr₂` into `X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G ×_{k̄} G`;

and then composes on the right with the **group-object difference morphism**
`GrpObj.diff G = (g, h) ↦ g · h⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G`, whose underlying scheme morphism
`(GrpObj.diff G).left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` is the honest group law `m ∘ (id × inv)`.

The pairing `prod` requires the source `X ×_{k̄} X` to be integral; this is passed
as the hypothesis `[IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)]`. The caller supplies it via
the project lemma `isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed` (self-product is smooth over
`k̄`, hence reduced) together with `GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace` — the
`isIntegral_pullback_self` recipe is spelled out in the module note below and lives
in `CodimOneExtension.lean`'s cone (it depends on the standard-smooth chart machinery
there, so it is not restated here to keep this file a Mathlib-only leaf).

## Main definitions

* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.diff` — the division morphism `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` of a group
  object in any cartesian-monoidal category.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.grpObjDiffLeft` — its underlying scheme morphism, typed as
  `pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.differenceRationalMap` — Milne's
  `Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G`.

## Main results

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self` / `..._snd_self` — the two
  projections of the self-product are open maps.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.differenceRationalMap_compHom_over` — the
  difference map is a `k̄`-rational map (`Φ.compHom G.hom = (pr₁ ≫ X.hom).toRat`).

Sub-steps 2 (`(x, x) ∈ Dom Φ ↔ x ∈ Dom f`) and 4b (diagonal codim-1 Krull bound)
remain; they consume `differenceRationalMap` built here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonoidalCategory Limits TopologicalSpace
open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory.GrpObj

variable {C : Type*} [Category C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]

/-- **Difference / division morphism of a group object.** For a group object `G`
in a cartesian-monoidal category, `GrpObj.diff G = fst / snd : G ⊗ G ⟶ G` is the
morphism `(g, h) ↦ g · h⁻¹`, i.e. the group law composed with inversion on the
second factor. There is no ready-made such morphism in mathlib (`GrpObj.conj` and
`GrpObj.commutator` are the only prebuilt `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` maps), so we build it from
the hom-set group structure `CategoryTheory.MonObj.Hom.group`. -/
noncomputable def diff (G : C) [GrpObj G] : G ⊗ G ⟶ G :=
  fst G G / snd G G

/-- **Reconstruction identity `(a · b⁻¹) · b = a` for `T`-points of a group object.**
Pairing `a` and `b` into `G ⊗ G`, applying the difference `diff G = fst / snd`
(which sends `(a, b) ↦ a · b⁻¹`), pairing the result again with `b`, and multiplying
recovers `a`. This is the group-theoretic heart of Milne Lemma 3.3 Sub-step 2, the
formula `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`: with `a = f(x)`, `b = f(u)`, the difference map value
`Φ = a · b⁻¹` recombines with `b` to give `a`. -/
lemma lift_diff_lift_mul {T : C} (G : C) [GrpObj G] (a b : T ⟶ G) :
    lift (lift a b ≫ diff G) b ≫ μ = a := by
  rw [diff, GrpObj.comp_div, lift_fst, lift_snd]
  exact div_mul_cancel a b

end CategoryTheory.GrpObj

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar]

/-- The underlying scheme morphism `(GrpObj.diff G).left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` of the
group-object difference morphism, typed directly against `pullback G.hom G.hom`
(definitionally `(G ⊗ G).left` via `Over.tensorObj_left`). This coercion avoids the
`(G ⊗ G).left` vs `pullback G.hom G.hom` transparency wall when right-composing a
rational map with target `pullback G.hom G.hom`. -/
noncomputable def grpObjDiffLeft (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left :=
  (GrpObj.diff G).left

/-- The difference morphism sits over `Spec k̄`: `grpObjDiffLeft G ≫ G.hom =
pr₁ ≫ G.hom`. This is the reduction that turns `Φ.compHom G.hom` into the structure
morphism of `X ×_{k̄} X`; it is `Over.w` of `GrpObj.diff G`. -/
lemma grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    grpObjDiffLeft G ≫ G.hom = pullback.fst G.hom G.hom ≫ G.hom :=
  Over.w (GrpObj.diff G)

/-- The underlying scheme morphism `μ.left : G ×_{k̄} G ⟶ G` of the group law of `G`,
typed against `pullback G.hom G.hom` (definitionally `(G ⊗ G).left`), mirroring
`grpObjDiffLeft`. -/
noncomputable def grpObjMulLeft (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G] :
    pullback G.hom G.hom ⟶ G.left :=
  (μ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G).left

/-- **Scheme-level reconstruction identity.** For two `k̄`-morphisms `A, B : T ⟶ G`
sharing the structure map `t` (`A ≫ G.hom = B ≫ G.hom = t`), pairing them, applying
the group difference `A · B⁻¹`, re-pairing with `B` and multiplying recovers `A`:
`m ∘ ⟨(A · B⁻¹), B⟩ = A`. This is `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.lift_diff_lift_mul`
transported through `Over.forget` (`(-).left` is a functor sending
`CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift`/`fst` to `pullback.lift`/`pullback.fst`); it is the
scheme incarnation of Milne's `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`. -/
lemma pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul (G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [GrpObj G]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) (A B : T ⟶ G.left)
    (hA : A ≫ G.hom = t) (hB : B ≫ G.hom = t) :
    pullback.lift (pullback.lift A B (hA.trans hB.symm) ≫ grpObjDiffLeft G) B
        (by rw [Category.assoc, grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom, ← Category.assoc,
          pullback.lift_fst, hA, hB]) ≫ grpObjMulLeft G
      = A := by
  have key := congrArg (fun m : Over.mk t ⟶ G => m.left)
    (GrpObj.lift_diff_lift_mul G (Over.homMk A hA) (Over.homMk B hB))
  simp only [Over.comp_left, Over.lift_left, Over.homMk_left] at key
  exact key

/-- The first projection `X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X` is an open map (it is smooth, being a
base change of the smooth structure morphism, hence universally open). -/
theorem isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self (X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth X.hom] :
    IsOpenMap (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).base :=
  (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).isOpenMap

/-- The second projection `X ×_{k̄} X ⟶ X` is an open map. -/
theorem isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self (X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth X.hom] :
    IsOpenMap (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).base :=
  (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).isOpenMap

namespace Scheme.RationalMap

/-- **Right-composition with a morphism only enlarges the domain of definition.**
For a rational map `F : X ⤏ Y` and a morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z`, every point at which
`F` is defined is also a point at which `F.compHom g` is defined: a partial-map
representative `F₀` of `F` yields the representative `F₀.compHom g` of
`F.compHom g` with the *same* domain (post-composing with a total morphism never
destroys definedness). This is Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 1: the difference map
`Φ = (prod ⋯).compHom (diff_G)` is defined wherever the pairing `prod ⋯` is. -/
theorem le_domain_compHom {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.RationalMap Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    F.domain ≤ (F.compHom g).domain := by
  intro x hx
  rw [RationalMap.mem_domain] at hx ⊢
  obtain ⟨F₀, hxF₀, hF₀⟩ := hx
  exact ⟨F₀.compHom g, hxF₀, by rw [RationalMap.compHom_toRationalMap, hF₀]⟩

variable {X G : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
  [Smooth X.hom]
  [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom]

/-- **Milne's difference rational map** `Φ = (x, y) ↦ f(x) · f(y)⁻¹`.

For a rational map `f : X ⤏ G` into a group variety over `k̄`, with `f` defined
over `k̄` (`f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap`), the difference map
`Φ : X ×_{k̄} X ⤏ G` is `((f ∘ pr₁) ×_{k̄} (f ∘ pr₂)) ∘ (g, h ↦ g · h⁻¹)`.

The self-product must be integral for the pairing `prod` to be well-defined; this
is the hypothesis `[IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)]`. -/
noncomputable def differenceRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (pullback X.hom X.hom).RationalMap G.left :=
  (RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
      (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
      (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap])
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
        pullback.condition])).compHom (grpObjDiffLeft G)

/-- **The difference map is a `k̄`-rational map.** Right-composing `Φ` with the
structure morphism `G.hom` recovers the structure morphism `pr₁ ≫ X.hom` of
`X ×_{k̄} X`. -/
theorem differenceRationalMap_compHom_over
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (differenceRationalMap f hover).compHom G.hom
      = (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom).toRationalMap := by
  simp only [differenceRationalMap]
  rw [RationalMap.compHom_compHom, grpObjDiffLeft_comp_hom]
  exact RationalMap.prod_compHom_over _ _ _ _ _ _ _

/-- The explicit pairing partial map `U ×_{k̄} U → G ×_{k̄} G` of Milne's
construction (`(x, y) ↦ (φ_U(x), φ_U(y))`), built from the maximal representative
`φ_U = f.toPartialMap` of `f` over the common domain `Dom(f∘pr₁) ⊓ Dom(f∘pr₂)`. It
is the partial-map witness that `prod` is defined on `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`. -/
noncomputable def precompDiffPairing
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left) (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (pullback X.hom X.hom).PartialMap (pullback G.hom G.hom) where
  domain := (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
      (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain
    ⊓ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
      (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).domain
  dense_domain := by
    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_inf]
    exact (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).dense_domain.inter_of_isOpen_left
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).dense_domain
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain.isOpen
  hom := pullback.lift
    ((pullback X.hom X.hom).homOfLE inf_le_left
      ≫ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).hom)
    ((pullback X.hom X.hom).homOfLE inf_le_right
      ≫ (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
        (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).hom)
    (by
      -- Over-`Spec k̄` structure making *both* projections `S`-morphisms (they agree
      -- after `X.hom` by `pullback.condition`), so the precomposed legs inherit
      -- over-ness from `f.toPartialMap` without ever unfolding `precomp`.
      letI : X.left.Over (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨X.hom⟩
      letI : G.left.Over (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨G.hom⟩
      letI : (pullback X.hom X.hom).Over (Spec (.of kbar)) :=
        ⟨pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom⟩
      haveI : f.IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := RationalMap.isOver_iff.mpr hover
      haveI : (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom).IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨rfl⟩
      haveI : (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom).IsOver (Spec (.of kbar)) := ⟨pullback.condition.symm⟩
      have e₁ : (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).hom ≫ G.hom
          = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain.ι ≫ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) :=
        (PartialMap.isOver_iff (S := Spec (.of kbar))).mp inferInstance
      have e₂ : (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).hom ≫ G.hom
          = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
            (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).domain.ι ≫ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) :=
        (PartialMap.isOver_iff (S := Spec (.of kbar))).mp inferInstance
      rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, e₁, e₂]
      simp only [← Category.assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_ι])

omit [GrpObj G] in
/-- The explicit pairing partial map represents Milne's `prod (f∘pr₁, f∘pr₂)`. Both
are `k̄`-rational maps out of the integral scheme `X ×_{k̄} X`, so it suffices to
match their induced morphisms `Spec K(X × X) ⟶ G ×_{k̄} G`: on each `pullback`
factor the pairing's generic-point morphism restricts to `(f ∘ prᵢ)`'s. -/
theorem precompDiffPairing_toRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (precompDiffPairing f hover).toRationalMap
      = RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
        (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
        (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap])
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
          pullback.condition]) := by
  refine RationalMap.eq_of_fromFunctionField_eq _ _ ?_
  rw [RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, prod_fromFunctionField]
  apply pullback.hom_ext
  · rw [pullback.lift_fst]
    have hrhs : (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField
        = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField := by
      rw [← RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, RationalMap.precomp_toRationalMap,
        f.toRationalMap_toPartialMap]
    rw [hrhs, ← PartialMap.fromFunctionField_restrict
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X))
      (precompDiffPairing f hover).dense_domain inf_le_left]
    simp only [PartialMap.fromFunctionField, PartialMap.fromSpecStalkOfMem,
      PartialMap.restrict_hom, Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
  · rw [pullback.lift_snd]
    have hrhs : (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField
        = (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom)
          (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField := by
      rw [← RationalMap.fromFunctionField_toRationalMap, RationalMap.precomp_toRationalMap,
        f.toRationalMap_toPartialMap]
    rw [hrhs, ← PartialMap.fromFunctionField_restrict
      (f.toPartialMap.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
      (precompDiffPairing f hover).dense_domain inf_le_right]
    simp only [PartialMap.fromFunctionField, PartialMap.fromSpecStalkOfMem,
      PartialMap.restrict_hom, Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 1 (domain lower bound / Sub-step 2 easy direction).**
The difference rational map `Φ` is defined on `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`: every point
`p` of `X ×_{k̄} X` projecting into `Dom(f)` under both projections lies in
`Dom(Φ)`. This is Milne's "clearly `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)` if `f` is defined at
`x`" — indeed at every `(x, y)` with `x, y ∈ Dom(f)` — made precise: a maximal
representative `(U, φ_U)` of `f` (`f.toPartialMap`) supplies the honest morphism
`U ×_{k̄} U → G` of Milne's construction, which represents `Φ`. -/
theorem le_domain_differenceRationalMap
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain) ⊓ (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain)
      ≤ (differenceRationalMap f hover).domain := by
  -- Right-composition with `diff_G` only enlarges the domain, reducing to `prod`;
  -- the explicit pairing `precompDiffPairing` is a representative defined on all of
  -- `Dom(f) ×_{k̄} Dom(f)`.
  refine le_trans ?_ (le_domain_compHom _ (grpObjDiffLeft G))
  intro p hp
  rw [RationalMap.mem_domain]
  exact ⟨precompDiffPairing f hover, hp, precompDiffPairing_toRationalMap f hover⟩

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 2 reconstruction identity.** `f ∘ pr₁ = m ∘ ⟨Φ, f ∘ pr₂⟩`:
the difference map `Φ = f(x)·f(y)⁻¹` recombined with the second factor `f ∘ pr₂` via the
group law `m` recovers the first factor `f ∘ pr₁`. This is Milne's formula
`f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)`, made a rational-map identity on `X ×_{k̄} X` via the
function-field group law (`pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul`). -/
theorem reconstruct_precomp_fst
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] :
    (RationalMap.prod (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom G.hom
        (differenceRationalMap f hover)
        (f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))
        (differenceRationalMap_compHom_over f hover)
        (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
          pullback.condition])).compHom (grpObjMulLeft G)
      = f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X) := by
  refine RationalMap.eq_of_fromFunctionField_eq _ _ ?_
  rw [RationalMap.fromFunctionField_compHom, RationalMap.prod_fromFunctionField]
  simp only [differenceRationalMap, RationalMap.fromFunctionField_compHom,
    RationalMap.prod_fromFunctionField]
  exact pullback_lift_diff_lift_mul G _
    ((f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).fromFunctionField)
    ((f.precomp (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X)).fromFunctionField)
    (RationalMap.fromFunctionField_comp_structure _ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap]))
    (RationalMap.fromFunctionField_comp_structure _ (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom ≫ X.hom) G.hom
      (by rw [RationalMap.precomp_compHom, hover, RationalMap.precomp_hom_toRationalMap,
        pullback.condition]))

/-- **Milne Lemma 3.3, Sub-step 2 (hard direction, algebraic content).** `f ∘ pr₁` is
defined wherever `Φ` is defined *and* `f ∘ pr₂` is defined: at a point `p` with
`Φ` defined and `pr₂ p ∈ Dom(f)`, the reconstruction `f(x) = Φ(x, u) · f(u)` exhibits
`f ∘ pr₁` as regular. Concretely `Dom(Φ) ⊓ pr₂⁻¹(Dom f) ≤ Dom(f ∘ pr₁)`.

This is the group-theoretic half of Milne's converse (`(x, x) ∈ Dom Φ ⟹ x ∈ Dom f`);
it remains to combine it with the topological input — openness of `Dom(Φ)` and
irreducibility of the fibre `X_{κ(x)}` (geometric irreducibility) to produce a suitable
`u`, plus the smooth-descent reflection `Dom(f ∘ pr₁) ⊆ pr₁⁻¹(Dom f)`. -/
theorem le_domain_precomp_fst_of_difference
    (f : X.left.RationalMap G.left)
    (hover : f.compHom G.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap)
    [IsIntegral (pullback X.hom X.hom)] [IsReduced X.left] [G.left.IsSeparated] :
    (differenceRationalMap f hover).domain ⊓ (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ f.domain)
      ≤ (f.precomp (pullback.fst X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_fst_self X)).domain := by
  rw [← reconstruct_precomp_fst f hover]
  refine le_trans ?_ (le_domain_compHom _ (grpObjMulLeft G))
  refine le_trans (inf_le_inf_left _ (RationalMap.le_domain_precomp f
    (pullback.snd X.hom X.hom) (isOpenMap_pullback_snd_self X))) ?_
  exact RationalMap.le_domain_prod _ _ _ _ _ _ _

end Scheme.RationalMap

end AlgebraicGeometry

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian

/-!
# The Abel-Jacobi map

The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian, and the universal property
of the Jacobian as the Albanese variety.

Since `Jacobian C` is by definition `(jacobianWitness C).J`, every declaration below is a
projection of the Albanese universal property carried by the witness field
`(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P : IsAlbanese C P (jacobianWitness C).J`.

## Main results

* `Jacobian.ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map `C ⟶ Jacobian C` attached to a `k`-rational point
  `P` of `C`.
* `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map sends `P` to the neutral element of
  `Jacobian C`.
* `Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`: a morphism `f : C ⟶ A` to an abelian variety with
  `P ≫ f = η[A]` factors uniquely through the Abel-Jacobi map.

## Remaining obligations

The genus-0 rigidity input (classical rigidity `Hom(ℙ¹, A) = A(k)`) is not proved here: it is
part of the existence claim `nonempty_jacobianWitness` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian`, which is
still open.  The `isAlbaneseFor` field of a witness must verify the Albanese property for
genus-0 curves too, which is exactly that rigidity content.

## References

Source: [Mumford], *Abelian Varieties*, §4 (rigidity).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
  [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

namespace Jacobian

variable {C} in
-- data
/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
to a `k`-rational point of `C`. Projects the Albanese universal morphism carried
by the witness `(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. -/
noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C := by
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).ofCurve

variable {C} in
/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η` below) is
the neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. Projects the pointed-property
of the Albanese witness `(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. -/
lemma comp_ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] := by
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).comp_ofCurve

variable {C} in
/--
The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`,
any morphism `f : C ⟶ A` such that `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the
Jacobian of `C`.
In other words, `Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.

The existence-and-uniqueness data is projected unconditionally from the witness
`(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. The genus-0 rigidity content (`Hom(ℙ¹, A) = A(k)`,
Mumford §4) is absorbed into the deferred existence claim `nonempty_jacobianWitness`,
since the witness must verify the Albanese property for genus-0 curves too.
-/
theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g := by
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).exists_unique_ofCurve_comp f hf

end Jacobian

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StructureSheafPushforward

/-!
# Rigidified relative Picard bundles (B1: the `RigidifiedPic` API)

For a relative curve `πC : C ⟶ S` with a **section of the projection**
`σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` (i.e. `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`, where `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`), Kleiman's
rigidification of the relative Picard functor replaces a bare line bundle `L` on
`C ×_S T` by a *rigidified* one — a bundle equipped with a trivialisation of its
restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T` along the section. Rigidified bundles have no non-trivial
automorphisms (`lm:aut`, the ring-level heart of which is
`StructureSheafPushforward.eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate`), so the
rigidified functor is a Zariski sheaf and represents the relative Picard functor.

This file supplies the substrate of that programme:

* `sectionPullbackProjIso` — the section base-change iso `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N` (from
  `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T` via the pullback pseudofunctor);
* `Rigidification σ L` — a trivialisation `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`;
* `exists_rigidification_relPicRel` — **Kleiman `lm:fff`**: every `L` is
  `H_T`-equivalent to a rigidified bundle `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`;
* `rationalPointSection` — the section `σ_T` of the projection produced by a
  `k`-rational point `x₀` of `C`, matching the hypothesis shape consumed by the
  `StructureSheafPushforward` `lm:aut` lemmas.

Blueprint references: Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, Lemmas `lm:fff` (existence of the
rigidified representative), `lm:aut` (automorphism-freeness). The `H_T`-relation
`PicSharp.relPicRel` is the one of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean`.
-/

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

namespace PicSharp

/-! ## §1. The section base-change isomorphism -/

/-- **Section base-change iso** `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N`.

For a section `σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`
(so `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`) and a sheaf of modules `N` on `T`, the pullback pseudofunctor
identity `(σ ≫ π_T)^* ≅ σ^* ∘ π_T^*` together with `𝟙_T^* ≅ id` identifies the
double pullback `σ^*(π_T^* N)` with `N`. This is the same three-step
`pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr`/`pullbackId` chain as `LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq`,
specialised to a section. -/

/-!
# Kernels of surjections of regular local rings are dim-difference generated

The diagonal-ideal brick of Milne Lemma 3.3, substep 4b-transport
(`informal/m33-spec.md` D5(a)/(c), point-agnostic form). Main result:

* `RingTheory.CohenMacaulay.exists_ofList_eq_ker_of_surjective` — for a
  surjective ring map `φ : B →+* A` of **regular local** Noetherian rings,
  the kernel is generated by `dim B − dim A` elements:
  there is a list `xs` with `Ideal.ofList xs = ker φ` and
  `xs.length + dim A = dim B` (stated with `spanFinrank` of the maximal
  ideals, which equals the Krull dimension by regularity; the
  `ringKrullDim` form is `…exists_ofList_eq_ker_length_add_ringKrullDim`).

The proof is a downward induction on `n = spanFinrank 𝔪_B`, entirely
two-residue-field-free:

* if `spanFinrank 𝔪_A = n`, then `coheight (ker φ) = dim (B/ker φ) = dim A
  = dim B`, so `ker φ` is a **minimal** prime (`coheight` strict
  antitonicity, `mem_minimalPrimes_of_coheight_eq_ringKrullDim`) of the
  **domain** `B` (landed `isDomain_of_regularLocal`), hence `ker φ = ⊥`;
* otherwise `spanFinrank 𝔪_A < n` forces some `x ∈ ker φ ∖ 𝔪_B²` — else
  lifts of generators of `𝔪_A` would generate `𝔪_B` modulo `𝔪_B²`, and
  Nakayama (`sup_eq_sup_smul_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson`) would give
  `spanFinrank 𝔪_B ≤ spanFinrank 𝔪_A`. The quotient `B/(x)` is again
  regular local with `spanFinrank` dropped by one (landed
  `regularLocal_quotient_isRegularLocal_of_notMemSq`), `φ` descends, and
  the inductive kernel generators lift along `Ideal.ker_quotient_lift` +
  `comap_map_of_surjective`.

The 4b-transport consumes this at the diagonal: for the closed immersion

A `#print axioms` on a declaration that *quantifies over* `[HasPicScheme C]`

1657	`Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` --- to the leading coefficient of the
1658	Hilbert polynomial of a representing invertible sheaf `L` on `C` (relative

1660	`χ(C, L ⊗ O_C(n)) = n · deg L + 1 - g`, so the degree is the leading
1661	coefficient of `Φ_L(n)`, well-defined on the isomorphism class `[L]` and on
1662	the `k`-point `λ` (because `PicScheme C` represents the étale-sheafified
1663	relative Picard functor).

1666	`Pic_{C/k}(k)` (tensor product on `L`) to `(ℤ, +)`; only the underlying
1667	function is stated here, the homomorphism property and the functoriality in

1672	project. Representability already transports a `k`-rational point to a relative Picard class

1674	sheaf extraction is needed — only a degree homomorphism on those classes, which is
1675	`ClassDegreePinned`.

1679	all; it would have to invent a value off the sections." The first clause does not follow from

1681	is *permitted* to do, and `fun _ => 0` already witnesses that the type is inhabited — so
1682	"cannot be built" was never true, and a `sorry` is not the honest encoding of "the domain is

1686	`Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` need not satisfy `lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙`, so it need

1691	* on sections it is `degreeOfSectionPinned`, i.e. *the* degree, pinned against the Abel map;

1693	
1694	`degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned` below records the first half as an equation, so the value
1695	on the rational points — the only place the classical degree map is defined — is determined
1696	rather than chosen. Consumers should still prefer `degreeOfSectionPinned`, which carries the
1697	section hypothesis in its type and therefore cannot be misread; `degree` exists because

1703	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1704	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1705	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C] :
1706	    (Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) → ℤ :=
1707	  fun lambda =>
1708	    if h : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) then
1709	      degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda h
1710	    else 0
1711	
1712	/-- **On a `k`-rational point, `degree` is the pinned degree** — the equation that makes

1715	Immediately `dif_pos`. Recorded as a named lemma because it is the whole content of the

1719	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1720	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StructureSheafPushforward

/-!
# Rigidified relative Picard bundles (B1: the `RigidifiedPic` API)

For a relative curve `πC : C ⟶ S` with a **section of the projection**
`σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` (i.e. `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`, where `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`), Kleiman's
rigidification of the relative Picard functor replaces a bare line bundle `L` on
`C ×_S T` by a *rigidified* one — a bundle equipped with a trivialisation of its
restriction `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T` along the section. Rigidified bundles have no non-trivial
automorphisms (`lm:aut`, the ring-level heart of which is
`StructureSheafPushforward.eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate`), so the
rigidified functor is a Zariski sheaf and represents the relative Picard functor.

This file supplies the substrate of that programme:

* `sectionPullbackProjIso` — the section base-change iso `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N` (from
  `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T` via the pullback pseudofunctor);
* `Rigidification σ L` — a trivialisation `σ^* L ≅ 𝒪_T`;
* `exists_rigidification_relPicRel` — **Kleiman `lm:fff`**: every `L` is
  `H_T`-equivalent to a rigidified bundle `L' = L ⊗ π_T^*((σ^* L)⁻¹)`;
* `rationalPointSection` — the section `σ_T` of the projection produced by a
  `k`-rational point `x₀` of `C`, matching the hypothesis shape consumed by the
  `StructureSheafPushforward` `lm:aut` lemmas.

Blueprint references: Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, Lemmas `lm:fff` (existence of the
rigidified representative), `lm:aut` (automorphism-freeness). The `H_T`-relation
`PicSharp.relPicRel` is the one of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean`.
-/

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

namespace PicSharp

/-! ## §1. The section base-change isomorphism -/

/-- **Section base-change iso** `σ^*(π_T^* N) ≅ N`.

For a section `σ : T ⟶ C ×_S T` of the projection `π_T = pullback.snd πC πT`
(so `σ ≫ π_T = 𝟙_T`) and a sheaf of modules `N` on `T`, the pullback pseudofunctor
identity `(σ ≫ π_T)^* ≅ σ^* ∘ π_T^*` together with `𝟙_T^* ≅ id` identifies the
double pullback `σ^*(π_T^* N)` with `N`. This is the same three-step
`pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr`/`pullbackId` chain as `LineBundle.pullback_pullback_eq`,
specialised to a section. -/

/-!

The diagonal-ideal brick of Milne Lemma 3.3, substep 4b-transport
(`informal/m33-spec.md` D5(a)/(c), point-agnostic form). Main result:

* `RingTheory.CohenMacaulay.exists_ofList_eq_ker_of_surjective` — for a
  surjective ring map `φ : B →+* A` of **regular local** Noetherian rings,
  the kernel is generated by `dim B − dim A` elements:
  there is a list `xs` with `Ideal.ofList xs = ker φ` and
  `xs.length + dim A = dim B` (stated with `spanFinrank` of the maximal
  ideals, which equals the Krull dimension by regularity; the
  `ringKrullDim` form is `…exists_ofList_eq_ker_length_add_ringKrullDim`).

The proof is a downward induction on `n = spanFinrank 𝔪_B`, entirely
two-residue-field-free:

* if `spanFinrank 𝔪_A = n`, then `coheight (ker φ) = dim (B/ker φ) = dim A
  = dim B`, so `ker φ` is a **minimal** prime (`coheight` strict
  antitonicity, `mem_minimalPrimes_of_coheight_eq_ringKrullDim`) of the
  **domain** `B` (landed `isDomain_of_regularLocal`), hence `ker φ = ⊥`;
* otherwise `spanFinrank 𝔪_A < n` forces some `x ∈ ker φ ∖ 𝔪_B²` — else
  lifts of generators of `𝔪_A` would generate `𝔪_B` modulo `𝔪_B²`, and
  Nakayama (`sup_eq_sup_smul_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson`) would give

  the inductive kernel generators lift along `Ideal.ker_quotient_lift` +
  `comap_map_of_surjective`.

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSheaf
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivFunctorDef
10	
11	/-!
12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302), and a
44	representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology. So an
45	unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a **false** statement, not
46	merely an unproved one. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
47	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
48	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
49	
50	```
51	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
52	```
53	
54	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as `PicEtComparisonIso`
55	(the use-site comparison class) and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, both clearly
56	labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not the headline
57	and must not be reported as progress toward it.
58	
59	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
60	
61	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
62	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
63	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
64	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
65	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
66	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
67	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
68	
69	## Main results
70	
71	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
72	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
73	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
74	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
75	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
76	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
77	* `PicEtComparisonIso`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — the **conditional**
78	  Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the challenge, not the
79	  headline.
80	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
81	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
82	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
83	  quotient encoding).
84	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
85	  scheme and the natural bijection
86	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
87	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
88	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
89	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
90	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
91	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
92	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
93	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
94	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
95	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
96	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
97	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
98	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
99	
100	## Remaining obligations
101	
102	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
103	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
104	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
105	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
106	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
107	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**: discharging it needs
108	`Div` representability (Kleiman §3 `th:repDiv`, blocked on Quot) and the
109	Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma. Everything else here — the representing scheme,
110	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
111	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
112	that one existence statement.
113	
114	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
115	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
116	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
117	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
118	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
119	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
120	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
121	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
122	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
123	
124	## References
125	
126	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
127	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
128	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
129	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
130	-/
131	
132	set_option autoImplicit false
133	
134	universe u
135	
136	open CategoryTheory Limits
137	
138	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
139	
140	namespace Scheme
141	
142	/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
143	section `σ : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
144	curves of this project this is the pointing `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ C`
145	already threaded through the Albanese statements (`AlgebraicJacobian.IsAlbanese`).
146	
147	This is the hypothesis of Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: together with
148	`O_S = f_* O_X` universally (automatic for proper geometrically integral
149	fibers), a section forces the comparison maps
150	`Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)` to be bijective, so
151	the *plain* relative Picard functor is already the étale sheaf that FGA
152	representability (Kleiman §4) represents. -/
153	class HasRationalPoint {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop where
154	  nonempty_section :
155	    Nonempty {σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left // σ ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))}
156	
157	namespace PicScheme
158	
159	/-! ## §0. The relative Picard functor and the divisor functor
160	
161	`picSharp` is the honest relative Picard functor of sibling
162	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2 Def `df:Pfs`), with the group
163	structure forgotten (representability is a statement about the underlying
164	set-valued functor; the group structure is transported back onto the
165	representing scheme by `groupSchemeStructure` below).
166	
167	`divFunctor` (the relative-effective-divisor functor `Div_{C/k}`, Kleiman §3
168	Def `df:div`) is the functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of sibling
169	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`. -/
170	
171	/-- **The relative Picard functor** `Pic^♯_{C/k} : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)`,
172	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` — the set-valued shadow of the group-valued
173	presheaf `PicSharp.relPresheaf` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (the honest
174	`H_T`-coset carrier of Kleiman §2 Def `df:Pfs`).
175	
176	Universe note: the values live in `Type (u+1)` because the line-bundle
177	carrier `LineBundle.OnProduct` is a quotient of (large) sheaves of modules.
178	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is universe-polymorphic, so representability by a
179	(`Type u`-homed) scheme remains a well-formed — and, under a rational point,
180	true — statement. -/
181	noncomputable def picSharp {k : Type u} [Field k]
182	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
183	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
184	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
185	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
186	
187	/-- Typeclass asserting existence of the relative-divisor functor `Div_{C/k}`.
188	The instance `instHasDivFunctor` below discharges it, with witness
189	`divFunctor C = DivFunctor C.hom`; the class survives as the blueprint-pinned
190	existence carrier (`def:has_div_functor`).
191	
192	**Vacuity warning.** The field
193	`has_div_functor : Nonempty ((Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1))` does not
194	mention `C` at all: any functor (e.g. a constant functor) witnesses it, so
195	the class is vacuously true and carries no mathematical content. It must
196	never be cited as evidence that the relative-divisor functor of `C` exists —
197	use `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) directly, as
198	`divFunctor` below does. -/
199	class HasDivFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop where
200	  has_div_functor : Nonempty ((Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1))
201	
202	/-- **The relative-divisor functor** `Div_{C/k} : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)`,
203	sending a `k`-scheme `T` to the set of relative effective Cartier divisors on
204	`C ×_k T` flat over `T` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`).
205	
206	It is defined as
207	
208	```
209	divFunctor C := Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom
210	```
211	
212	with `Scheme.DivFunctor` from sibling `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`: `T`-flat
213	invertible-kernel quotients of `O_{C ×_k T}` modulo `ker q = ker q'`, i.e.
214	Kleiman's set of relative effective divisors. The definition does not route
215	through the `HasDivFunctor` carrier class above. -/
216	noncomputable def divFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
217	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
218	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
219	  DivFunctor C.hom
220	
221	/-- Existence instance for `HasDivFunctor`: the relative-divisor functor
222	`divFunctor C = Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` witnesses the existential. -/
223	instance instHasDivFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
224	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : HasDivFunctor C :=
225	  ⟨⟨divFunctor C⟩⟩
226	
227	end PicScheme
228	
229	/-! ## §1. The Picard scheme
230	
231	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` of a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
232	`C/k` **with a `k`-rational point** is the `k`-scheme representing the
233	relative Picard functor `picSharp C` (which, under the rational point, agrees
234	with the étale-sheafified functor of Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` by Kleiman §2
235	Thm 2.5). The scheme is separated, locally of finite type over `k`, and a
236	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes; the
237	abelian-group-scheme structure is `groupSchemeStructure` below.
238	
239	Blueprint reference: `def:pic_scheme` (Kleiman §4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/
240	
241	/-- Typeclass asserting existence of a scheme over `Spec k` that represents
242	the **unsheafified** relative Picard functor `picSharp C` and is separated and
243	locally of finite type over `k`.
244	
245	**This is the legacy, conditional interface, not the headline target.** Its only
246	producer is `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, which needs both
247	`[HasRationalPoint C]` and the comparison class `PicEtComparisonIso C`, and
248	there is deliberately **no instance**: without a section the plain relative
249	functor is not representable in general, so an unconditional instance would
250	assert a false statement. The unconditional étale target is `HasPicSchemeEt`.
251	
252	Consumers that quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain
253	kernel-clean and valid; what they prove are conditional statements until
254	restated against `picEt`.
255	
256	Representability, local finiteness and separatedness are bundled into a single
257	existential because Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) delivers them as one package:
258	`Pic_{C/k}` is a separated scheme locally of finite type over `k`, a disjoint
259	union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes. Bundling therefore adds no
260	strength beyond representability, and lets the carriers
261	`PicScheme.instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` and `PicScheme.isSeparated` be
262	obtained by extraction. -/
263	class HasPicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
264	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
265	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
266	  has_pic_scheme : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
267	    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
268	      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom
269	
270	/-- The **Picard scheme** `Pic_{C/k}` of a smooth proper geometrically
271	integral curve `C/k`, encoded as an object of `Over (Spec (.of k))`.
272	
273	Extracted (`Classical.choose`) from the `HasPicScheme` existence field, so it
274	carries the identity "this scheme represents the relative Picard functor
275	`picSharp C`" through `representable` below — a natural bijection onto
276	`Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`. -/
277	noncomputable def PicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
278	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
280	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
281	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
282	  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose
283	
284	/-- **THE PROJECT'S CENTRAL OPEN OBLIGATION — expected to stay open.**
285	
286	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch`: for a smooth proper geometrically
287	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
288	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
289	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
290	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
291	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
292	why they are bundled.
293	
294	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
295	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
296	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
297	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
298	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
299	labelled as strictly weaker.
300	
301	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
302	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
303	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
304	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
305	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
306	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
307	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
308	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
309	
310	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
311	Discharging it means formalising the Kleiman §4 existence proof: the Abel-map
312	slice `Div^d_{C/k} → Pic^d_{C/k}` is a smooth proper equivalence relation whose
313	quotient is a scheme (`smoothProperQuotient`, itself gated on
314	`HasSmoothProperQuotient` because Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity
315	vocabulary), together with `Div` representability (Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`,
316	which needs the Quot scheme). Neither input is available; the project reaches
317	this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single named `sorry` that
318	the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with a weaker
319	conditional statement to make a count go down.
320	
321	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
322	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
323	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison class
324	`PicEtComparisonIso` and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is
325	derived from it.
326	
327	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
328	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
329	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
330	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
331	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
332	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
333	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
334	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
335	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
336	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
337	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
338	than asserting it. -/
339	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability {k : Type u} [Field k]
340	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
341	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
342	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :

514	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
515	
516	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
517	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
518	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
519	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
520	
521	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
522	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/

530	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
531	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
532	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
533	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
534	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
535	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
536	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
537	negation on the group-valued functor.

539	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
540	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
541	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
542	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose

544	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
545	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation

548	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available

555	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
