700	/-! ## §3. The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent
701	
702	The structural lemma underlying Step 4 of Kleiman §4 Thm. `th:main`: given a
703	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
704	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
705	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.
706	
707	The hypothesis list expressible here is strictly weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem
708	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
709	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
710	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
711	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
712	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
713	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
714	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural
715	transformation is representable.
716	
717	`HasSmoothProperQuotient α` is therefore an **explicit use-site hypothesis**:

752	(4) `α` an étale-local surjection (every `T`-point of `P` lifts along some

778	
779	Grothendieck's existence theorem for the Picard scheme (Kleiman §4 Thm.
780	`th:main`, specialised via Cor. `cor:algsch` to `S = Spec k`, `X = C`),
781	transported through Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 to the plain relative functor under

793	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
794	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
795	  has_representable : Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C))
796

798	`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component

811	`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
812	point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
813	the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection
814	
815	```
816	(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
817	```

830	/-! ## §5. The abelian group-scheme structure
831	
832	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` inherits an abelian group-scheme structure from
833	the tensor product of invertible sheaves on `C ×_k T`: the relative Picard
834	presheaf is group-valued (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), and a representing object
835	of (the set-valued shadow of) a group-valued presheaf is canonically a group
836	object, by Yoneda transport (`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`).
837	
838	Since `picSharp` is by definition `relPresheaf ⋙ forget`, the transport
839	applies directly.
840	
841	Blueprint reference: `thm:pic_is_group_scheme` (Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs` +
842	§4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/

844	/-- The multiplicative (`CommGrpCat`-valued) avatar of the relative Picard
845	presheaf, used to feed `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (whose API is
846	multiplicative). Carrier-level it is the same functor: `Multiplicative` is a
847	type synonym. -/
848	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
849	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
850	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
851	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
852	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
853	
854	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picSharpCommGrp` and `picSharp` agree up to
855	the canonical `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection (a natural isomorphism, since
856	`Multiplicative` is carrier-preserving). -/
857	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
858	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
859	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
860	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
861	  NatIso.ofComponents
862	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
863	      (α := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
864	    (fun _ => rfl)
865	
866	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
867	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,
868	obtained by Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the
869	abelian-group structure of the relative Picard presheaf
870	`PicSharp.relPresheaf` along the representability witness `representable C`.
871	Concretely: `[L] + [M] = [L ⊗ M]`, `-[L] = [L⁻¹]`, unit `[O_{C ×_k T}]`,
872	transported through `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`.
873	
874	Commutativity comes for free from the transport, so this is the full
875	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
876	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
877	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
878	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
879	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
880	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
881	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
882	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)
883	    ((representable C).ofIso (picSharpCommGrpForgetIso C))

919	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
920	    PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C :=
921	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1⟩

928	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
929	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
930	    [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :

1	/-

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AbelianVariety
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.CodimOneExtension
10	
11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	**Status, measured (run 0069).** `albanese_universal_property` is *assembled*
54	from `descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`,
55	and that assembly is honest — but the headline is **not** sorry-free:
56	`#print axioms albanese_universal_property` reports `sorryAx`, inherited from
57	the six unproved declarations below. It should not be described as a landed
58	theorem until they close.
59	
60	### Read this first: the mathematics is proved *elsewhere in this directory*
61	
62	The six obligations below are stated against `SymmetricPower`, which is a
63	`sorry`-**bodied definition**. An equation between morphisms out of a junk term
64	carries no information, so these six cannot be discharged, and discharging them
65	would establish nothing. They are kept because they pin the challenge's intended
66	statement shape, not because they are the work.
67	
68	Milne's argument itself **is** proved, over the symmetric power taken as an
69	*interface* rather than a `sorry`:
70	
71	* `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean` — `SymPowData C n` (carrier, symmetrisation
72	  projection, universal property), and everything Milne derives from it:
73	  `SymPowData.symAVMap` (his `Sym^n φ`, now a **construction**),
74	  `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` (the collapse behind "use `φ(P₀) = η_A`"),
75	  and `symPowDataOne` — which **inhabits** the interface (`Sym^1 C = C`), so
76	  statements quantifying over it are not vacuous.
77	* `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` — the connector in **both** directions and the
78	  universal property assembled over the interface. Worth knowing: the backward
79	  direction needs neither the quotient property nor that `ψ` is a homomorphism;
80	  only the forward direction does.
81	* `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean` — commutativity of an abelian variety and pointed
82	  rigidity, on the project's four-instance package.
83	* `Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean` — the instantiation at `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`, plus a
84	  machine check attributing its `sorryAx` entirely to the Picard seam: the same
85	  theorem with an arbitrary abelian variety target is axiom-clean.
86	
87	So the honest description of this leg is **one missing object**, not six gaps:
88	`SymPowData C g` for `g ≥ 2`.
89	
90	**Update (2026-07-28) — that object is now identified, and the missing part is smaller than
91	this paragraph used to say.** `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` proves that `SymPowData C n`
92	*together with* its symmetry hypothesis **is** a colimit of the `S_n`-action on `C^n`, in
93	both directions (`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff`), so:
94	
95	* the symmetry half is `colimit.w` — free, at every `n`;
96	* the **affine algebra** case is *inhabited* at every `n` (`symPowData_affineAlgebra`, in
97	  `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`), with no construction written. Identifying the carrier as
98	  `Spec (A^{⊗ n})^{S_g}` is expected but **not proved** — see that file's §5 header;
99	* what remains is the **gluing**, as one instance: `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` — the
100	  colimit of the `S_g`-action on `C^g`, for this curve and this `g`. Do **not** state the
101	  residue as `HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme`: that quantified
102	  form is strictly stronger, is not what `hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` covers, and is
103	  believed false at this pin, so a theorem carrying it would be vacuous.
104	
105	The `analogies/m3-route-audit.md` figure of 2400–3800 lines priced the affine-and-glue
106	route as a whole (action typeclass, affine quotient with its universal property, glued
107	global quotient, smoothness). The first two are cheaper than that figure implies — the
108	affine-algebra quotient and its universal property come from mathlib's colimits — though
109	identifying the carrier and gluing remain. Treat the figure as historical and read
110	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` before budgeting from it.
111	
112	What *has* landed, and is genuinely unconditional, is the rational-map
113	extension this file consumes: `Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av` (Milne Theorem
114	3.2) is proved and axiom-clean as of run 0069, Milne Lemma 3.3 with it. So
115	`descentThroughBirationalSigma`'s *extension* step has a real input; what it
116	still lacks is the birationality data to build the rational map in the first
117	place (mathlib at this pin has no "invert a birational morphism on a dense
118	open" API).
119	
120	The six declarations stated without proof:
121	
122	* `abelJacobi` — the moduli classifier of the rigidified diagonal
123	  correspondence `𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`, taken as a
124	  relative degree-zero line bundle over the second factor.
125	* `SymmetricPower` — the affine-and-glue construction `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`
126	  of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11). Mathlib has
127	  no scheme-theoretic symmetric power, only `Sym` for types and modules.
128	* `symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the two invocations
129	  of the universal property of `Sym^g C`, which need the symmetric projection
130	  `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` supplied by that construction. Their *symmetric input* is
131	  proved (`MonObj.powSum` / `MonObj.powSum_perm`, `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`);
132	  only the factorisation through `π` is missing.
133	* `descentThroughBirationalSigma` — extension of the rational map
134	  `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` to a regular morphism (Milne Theorem I.3.2). The
135	  extension theorem `extend_to_av` is now proved and unconditional; the gap is
136	  upstream of it — producing the rational map, which needs the dense open on
137	  which `f^{(g)}` is an isomorphism *and* a way to invert it there.
138	* `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — Milne's identification of `ι_{P₀}`
139	  with `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`.
140	
141	## The scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
142	
143	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
144	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its
145	four abelian-variety attributes (`GrpObj`, `IsProper`, `Smooth`,
146	`GeometricallyIrreducible`), the carrier `Pic0.bundle C`, and the derived
147	definition `Pic0.jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme`.
148	
149	The upstream declarations `Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
150	geometricallyIrreducible}` run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,

theorem kPoints_iff_kerDegree {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.ClassDegreePinned C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
    Nonempty (Σ' (inc : (Pic0Scheme C).left ⟶ (PicScheme C).left),
      ∀ (lambda : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left),
        (∃ mu : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (Pic0Scheme C).left, mu ≫ inc = lambda) ↔
          PicScheme.degree C lambda = 0) :=
  sorry

/-- **A `k`-rational point of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is a `k`-rational point of `Pic_{C/k}`** —
sorry-free, and the piece `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` needs to even *state* its own conclusion on
the correct domain.

If `mu` is a section of `(Pic0Scheme C).hom` and `f` is a morphism over `Spec k` (in
particular the inclusion of `Pic0Scheme.inclusion`), then `mu ≫ f.left` is a section of
`(PicScheme C).hom`: associativity plus `Over.w f` plus the section equation.

Why this is worth a name: `PicScheme.degreeOfSection` — unlike the broken
`PicScheme.degree` — requires its argument to *be* a section, so any statement of the form
"points of `Pic⁰` are the degree-zero points" must produce that section proof for the
composite. This is it, and it is free. -/
theorem isSection_comp_inclusion {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
    (f : Pic0Scheme C ⟶ PicScheme C)
    (mu : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (Pic0Scheme C).left)
    (hmu : mu ≫ (Pic0Scheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    (mu ≫ f.left) ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) := by
  rw [Category.assoc, Over.w f, hmu]

/-- **The degree-zero characterisation of `Pic⁰`-points, on the correct domain** — the
restatement of `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` against `degreeOfSection` rather than the broken
`degree`, with its structural half discharged.

Compared with `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` above, three things are fixed or supplied here:

* the inclusion is `Pic0Scheme.inclusion`-style but taken as a morphism *over* `Spec k`, so
  that composing with it preserves sections (`isSection_comp_inclusion`);
* points are sections, matching `degreeOfSection`'s domain;
* the "⟹" direction is reduced to a statement purely about *classes*: a point coming from
  `Pic⁰` has trivial relative Picard class. Given that, degree zero is `map_zero`
  (`PicScheme.degreeOfSection_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero`).

The remaining hypothesis `hclass` is the honest mathematical content of Milne III.1 p.~88 in
this direction: the identity component consists of the classes of degree zero, i.e. the
degree map's kernel is exactly the connected component of the identity. It is *not*
bookkeeping — it is the statement that the degree separates the components of `Pic_{C/k}` —
which is why it is a hypothesis rather than a proof step. -/

    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] [PicScheme.ClassDegree C]
    (f : Pic0Scheme C ⟶ PicScheme C)

1654	/-- The **degree map** `Pic_{C/k}(k) → ℤ`.
1655	
1656	Sends a `k`-point `λ ∈ Pic_{C/k}(k)` --- a morphism
1657	`Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` --- to the leading coefficient of the
1658	Hilbert polynomial of a representing invertible sheaf `L` on `C` (relative
1659	to a fixed degree-one polarisation `O_C(1)`). By Riemann--Roch,
1660	`χ(C, L ⊗ O_C(n)) = n · deg L + 1 - g`, so the degree is the leading
1661	coefficient of `Φ_L(n)`, well-defined on the isomorphism class `[L]` and on
1662	the `k`-point `λ` (because `PicScheme C` represents the étale-sheafified
1663	relative Picard functor).
1664	
1665	The degree map is a group homomorphism from the additive structure on
1666	`Pic_{C/k}(k)` (tensor product on `L`) to `(ℤ, +)`; only the underlying
1667	function is stated here, the homomorphism property and the functoriality in
1668	`k` being left to separate lemmas.
1669	
1670	ROUTE CHANGE (run 0067). The construction is not the *Quot* obligation the original
1671	docstring described, and the difference matters because Quot is retained-not-revived in this
1672	project. Representability already transports a `k`-rational point to a relative Picard class
1673	over the base (`classOfSection`, sorry-free), so no Hilbert polynomial and no representing
1674	sheaf extraction is needed — only a degree homomorphism on those classes, which is
1675	`ClassDegreePinned`.
1676	
1677	**CLOSED (run 0067 r4), and the docstring this replaces was wrong on a point of fact.**
1678	It read: "A total function of that type therefore cannot be built from the Picard functor at
1679	all; it would have to invent a value off the sections." The first clause does not follow from
1680	the second. Inventing a value off the sections is exactly what a total function of this type
1681	is *permitted* to do, and `fun _ => 0` already witnesses that the type is inhabited — so
1682	"cannot be built" was never true, and a `sorry` is not the honest encoding of "the domain is
1683	wrong".
1684	
1685	What IS true is the observation the old note was reaching for: a morphism
1686	`Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` need not satisfy `lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙`, so it need
1687	not name a `k`-*rational* point, and representability says nothing about it. That is a
1688	statement about which values are *pinned*, not about totality. So the construction below
1689	splits on precisely that condition:
1690	
1691	* on sections it is `degreeOfSectionPinned`, i.e. *the* degree, pinned against the Abel map;
1692	* off them it is `0`, an arbitrary choice that no consumer may rely on.
1693	
1694	`degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned` below records the first half as an equation, so the value
1695	on the rational points — the only place the classical degree map is defined — is determined
1696	rather than chosen. Consumers should still prefer `degreeOfSectionPinned`, which carries the
1697	section hypothesis in its type and therefore cannot be misread; `degree` exists because
1698	`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` is stated against it, and it now has a body rather than a `sorry`.
1699	
1700	The `[ClassDegreePinned C]` binder is new and is what makes the pinned half meaningful; the
1701	unpinned `ClassDegree` would have permitted the zero homomorphism (see its docstring). -/
1702	noncomputable def degree {k : Type u} [Field k]
1703	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1704	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1705	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C] :
1706	    (Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) → ℤ :=
1707	  fun lambda =>
1708	    if h : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) then
1709	      degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda h
1710	    else 0
1711	
1712	/-- **On a `k`-rational point, `degree` is the pinned degree** — the equation that makes
1713	`degree`'s value on the sections determined rather than chosen.
1714

1716	claim that `degree` is a degree: off the sections its value is arbitrary, and this lemma

1718	theorem degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned {k : Type u} [Field k]
1719	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1720	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1721	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C]
1722	    (lambda : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left)
1723	    (hlambda : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
1724	    degree C lambda = degreeOfSectionPinned C lambda hlambda := by
1725	  classical
1726	  rw [degree, dif_pos hlambda]

1734	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1735	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1736	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [ClassDegreePinned C]
1737	    (lambda : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left)
1738	    (hlambda : lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
1739	    (hclass : classOfSection C lambda hlambda = 0) :

226	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
227	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=

9	/-!
10	# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map
11	
12	Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
13	degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
14	(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
15	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
16	functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
17	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).
18	
19	## The fibre degree
20	
21	For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
22	encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
23	the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is
24	
25	  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
26	
27	Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
28	`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.
29	
30	**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
31	finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
32	in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
33	B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
34	the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
35	an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
36	form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
37	value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
38	for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
39	`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
40	`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.
41	
42	**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
43	`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
44	the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
45	extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
46	support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
47	proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
48	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
49	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
50	`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
51	still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
52	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
53	degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
54	"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).
55	
56	## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form
57	
58	**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
59	"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
60	with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
61	piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
62	honest pins delivered here are:
63	
64	* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
65	  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
66	  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
67	  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
68	* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
69	  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
70	  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
71	* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
72	  nonempty `T`).
73	
74	The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
75	This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
76	proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
77	with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
78	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
79	current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
80	engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
81	pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
82	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
83	statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
84	`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
85	one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
86	for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
87	locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
88	general and by the degree only over curves.
89	
90	## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)
91	
92	**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
93	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.
94	
95	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —
96	
97	a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
98	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
99	`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
100	`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
101	`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
102	`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.
103	
104	**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
105	rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
106	vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
107	(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
108	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
109	line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
110	regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:
111	
112	* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
113	  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
114	  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
115	  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
116	  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
117	  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
118	* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
119	  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
120	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`
121	  (`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel`,
122	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`).
123	
124	In χ-ledger terms this is exactly `deg_t(ker q) = χ(I_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −d`;
125	the translation becomes a theorem once P3 lands.
126	
127	## References
128	
129	Blueprint: to be attached to the campaign's D1'/A2 nodes.

131	(Def. `df:div`, Def. `dfn:Abel`, Ex. `ex:DivC`); Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*,
132	II §5 (finite flat pushforward, for the gate's discharge route);
133	Stacks 02KH (`i = 0`) for the base-change core.
134	-/

153	`π₀.fiber s` induces a `κ(s)`-linear equivalence on global sections
154	(evaluation at `⊤` is functorial, and the `κ(s)`-scalar action factors through
155	`Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`), so the `κ(s)`-dimensions agree.  Twist-free

159	lemma finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso {W B : Scheme.{u}} (π₀ : W ⟶ B) (s : B)
160	    {G G' : (π₀.fiber s).Modules} (e : G ≅ G') :
161	    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
162	     Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G, ⊤))
163	      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
164	         Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G', ⊤)) := by
165	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
166	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
167	  have γe := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (π₀.fiber s) ⋙
168	    PresheafOfModules.evaluation (π₀.fiber s).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
169	      e).toLinearEquiv
170	  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
171	    { toFun := γe
172	      map_add' := γe.map_add
173	      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
174	      invFun := γe.symm
175	      left_inv := γe.left_inv
176	      right_inv := γe.right_inv }

368	            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
369	              (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)))

372	              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map

378	
379	/-- A divisor family **has (constant) fibre degree `d`** when every fibre
380	divisor has degree `d` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`).  Vacuously true for every

382	pairwise disjoint only over nonempty bases (`ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`). -/
383	def HasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
384	  ∀ t : (T.left : Scheme.{u}), x.fiberDeg t = d

389	theorem Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
390	    (d : ℕ) : x.HasFiberDeg d ↔ y.HasFiberDeg d :=
391	  forall_congr' fun t => by rw [h.fiberDeg_eq t]

394	slice `DivFunctorDeg` is a subfunctor, not just a sub-presheaf-of-sets.

396	theorem HasFiberDeg.pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} {x : DivFamily π T} {d : ℕ}

398	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).HasFiberDeg d :=
399	  fun t' => (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hx (ψ.left.base t'))

402	`Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)` — the carrier predicate of
403	`DivFunctorDeg π d`.  Well defined by `Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff`. -/
404	def ClassHasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (d : ℕ)
405	    (z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)) : Prop :=
406	  Quotient.liftOn z (fun x => x.HasFiberDeg d)
407	    fun _ _ h => propext (h.hasFiberDeg_iff d)

411	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x) ↔ x.HasFiberDeg d :=
412	  Iff.rfl

415	functoriality input of `DivFunctorDeg`. -/
416	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.map {T T' : Over S} {d : ℕ}
417	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)} (hz : ClassHasFiberDeg d z)
418	    (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
419	    ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.map (DivFamily.pullbackAlong ψ)
420	      (fun _ _ h => DivFamily.pullbackAlong_rel ψ h) z) := by
421	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
422	  | _ x =>
423	    intro t'
424	    exact (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hz (ψ.left.base t'))

427	pieces of `DivFunctor` are pairwise disjoint on nonempty `T` (and only there:
428	at `T = ∅` every class has every degree, see the module docstring audit). -/
429	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.unique {T : Over S}
430	    (hne : Nonempty (T.left : Scheme.{u})) {d d' : ℕ}
431	    {z : Quotient (DivFamily.setoid π T)}
432	    (h : ClassHasFiberDeg d z) (h' : ClassHasFiberDeg d' z) : d = d' := by
433	  induction z using Quotient.ind with
434	  | _ x =>
435	    obtain ⟨t⟩ := hne
436	    exact (h t).symm.trans (h' t)
437	
438	/-- **Degree side of the A2 sign audit** (rank vocabulary — see the module
439	docstring audit): a representative of a degree-`d` divisor class has, at
440	every point `t` of `T`, fibre ideal of colength `d`:
441	
442	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = d`.

444	Combined with the sign convention `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` of the Abel map
445	(`PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk`) this is the honest content of "the ideal sheaf
446	`ker q` of a rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" available before the P3
447	χ-ledger lands. -/
448	theorem ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel {T : Over S} {d : ℕ}
449	    (x : DivFamily π T)
450	    (hx : ClassHasFiberDeg d (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid π T) x))
451	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
452	    (letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
453	        (Limits.cokernel
454	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
455	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)))
456	     Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)

458	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
459	            (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)), ⊤))
460	      = d :=
461	  (x.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel t).symm.trans (hx t)

490	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))

492	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
493	    ext z
494	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f => ((TypeCat.Hom.hom f : TypeCat.Fun _ _) : _ → _))
495	      ((DivFunctor π).map_comp g h)) z.1

612	Mathematical content (TRUE at this pinned generality; Mumford, *Abelian
613	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): for a smooth proper relative
614	curve `C/k` and any `T`, a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` is finite
615	flat over `T` (proper + quasi-finite: each `D_t` is the zero scheme of a
616	regular section of an invertible ideal on the curve `C_t`, hence

618	`DivFamily.fiberDeg` — is Zariski-locally constant.  Discharge route: the

626	decomposition theorems are also available in hypothesis-parametrized form

396

400	morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` characterised on `T`-points by the
401	formula `(1 × ι_{P₀})^* 𝓜^{P₀} ≈ 𝓛^{P₀}`, where `𝓜^{P₀}` is the
402	Poincaré–Picard correspondence on `C × Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` and
403	`𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`.

406	of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`def:pic_scheme` together with its identity-component
407	refinement) to the relative degree-zero line bundle `𝓛^{P₀}` on
408	`C × C → C` along the second projection; Yoneda then produces the
409	unique classifying morphism `C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. The basepoint
